slides.title: Prerequisites
content: No prior AI or programming knowledge
slides.narration: This tutorial is for beginners. Some basic understanding of computers is helpful. No prior knowledge of AI or programming is needed.

slides.title: What is a Neural Network?
slides.narration: Have you heard of Artificial Intelligence? Neural Networks are a core part of AI. They are inspired by how our brains work. Think of them as a brain for computers. They help computers learn and make decisions.
slides.image_prompt: Stylized graphic of a human brain next to a simplified network of interconnected nodes.

slides.title: The Neuron: Building Block
content: Basic unit of a neural network.
Receives input, processes it, produces output.
slides.narration: Our brain has billions of neurons. Neural networks have artificial neurons. Each artificial neuron is a simple processor. It takes information in. It processes this information. Then it sends out a new signal.
slides.image_prompt: Simple illustration of a single artificial neuron with multiple inputs, a processing unit, and a single output. Arrows showing input flow to output.

slides.title: How Neurons Connect: Layers
slides.narration: These neurons connect in layers. First, we have an Input Layer. This is where data enters the network. Then come one or more Hidden Layers. These layers do the main processing. Finally, there is an Output Layer. This layer gives the network's final answer.
slides.image_prompt: Diagram showing three distinct layers of artificial neurons: an input layer (left), one hidden layer (middle), and an output layer (right), with lines connecting neurons between adjacent layers.

slides.title: How a Neuron Works: Inputs & Weights
slides.narration: Let's look closer at one neuron. It receives several inputs. Think of these as pieces of information. Each input has a 'weight'. Weights decide how important each input is. A higher weight means more importance.
slides.image_prompt: Close-up of a single artificial neuron. Multiple input lines (with small numbers representing weights on each line) converging into the neuron.

slides.title: How a Neuron Works: Activation
slides.narration: The neuron adds up all its inputs. It multiplies each input by its weight first. Then it applies an 'activation function'. This function decides if the neuron should 'fire'. Firing means sending a signal to the next layer. It's like deciding if enough evidence is present.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of a single artificial neuron. Inputs with weights entering. A sum symbol inside the neuron. An arrow pointing to an "Activation Function" box, then an output line.

slides.title: Learning from Data: Training
slides.narration: So, how do they learn? We 'train' them with lots of data. Think of data as examples. The network makes a guess or prediction. We compare its guess to the correct answer. If it's wrong, it adjusts its weights slightly. It keeps adjusting until its guesses are good.
slides.image_prompt: Graphic showing a cycle: Data input -> Neural Network (making prediction) -> Comparison with actual answer -> Feedback loop to "Adjust Weights" in the network.

slides.title: Analogy: Identifying Fruit
slides.narration: Let's use an analogy. Imagine teaching a child to identify fruit. You show them an apple. You say, "This is an apple." The child learns features: red, round, small stem. Next time, they see a red, round fruit. They guess "apple". If wrong, you correct them. They adjust their 'internal rules'.
slides.image_prompt: Split screen: A human teaching a child to identify fruits (pointing at an apple). On the other side, a diagram of a neural network with inputs like "red", "round", "small" and outputs like "apple", "banana".

slides.title: What Can Neural Networks Do?
slides.narration: Neural networks are used everywhere. They recognize faces in photos. They understand your voice commands. They translate languages for you. They recommend movies or products. They power self-driving cars. They are very versatile.
slides.image_prompt: Collage of icons representing various AI applications: a camera with a face outline, a microphone icon, a speech bubble with different language flags, a "recommended" star icon, a car icon.

slides.title: Summary
content: Made of interconnected neurons in layers.
Learn by adjusting weights from data.
slides.narration: In this tutorial, we learned about neural networks. They are inspired by the human brain. They consist of layers of artificial neurons. Each neuron processes inputs with weights. They learn by adjusting these weights. This happens during training with data. Neural networks power many AI applications.
slides.image_prompt: A summary slide with key points listed and a subtle background image of a neural network.

slides.title: Assignment
content: Reflect on an AI application you use daily.
How might a neural network be involved?
Think about its inputs and outputs.
slides.narration: Now for a practice task. Think of an AI application you use every day. For example, a voice assistant or a recommendation system. Consider how a neural network might work inside it. What kind of data would be its inputs? What kind of output would it produce? Share your thoughts with a friend.
slides.image_prompt: An icon of a thought bubble with a question mark, representing reflection and critical thinking.
